primary_analysis.reason: One value per state/UT (closest to independent observations); 'generated' is the headline metric and the same kind of figure as the CRDT calibration; the 2021-22 'generated' column has no excluded cells and matches the report's TOTAL row exactly; 2021-22 is the most recent report with the most entities. Fixed before any digit statistic was computed. Expected power is low (n~36).

result.label: PRIMARY: 2021-22 generated
caveats: 'conforms' means no statistically significant deviation at alpha; it is not proof the data is genuine.
'does_not_conform' is a reason to inspect, not proof of fabrication: genuine data can deviate (e.g. caps, minimums, rounding by measuring equipment, narrow ranges, few distinct sources).
n = 36 is below 110, so some expected digit counts are < 5; the p-value is simulated (20000 multinomial draws from Benford at the same n), not asymptotic.
low power: at n = 36, even leading digits that are completely uniform would be detected only 60% of the time at alpha = 0.01; a 'conforms' verdict here is weak evidence.

repeats.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

exact_repeats_consecutive_years.caution: A repeated figure can have innocent causes (e.g. an estimate carried forward unchanged, a population-based norm not updated, a state re-submitting last year's figure). It is not evidence of fabrication, and no rate of repeats 'expected by chance' is claimed here.

interpretation_limits: State totals are a different data-generating process from ward-level trip logs; conformity or non-conformity here says little about whether ward trip logs would follow Benford's Law.
With n ~ 36 per year x metric, power is low: 'conforms' is weak evidence of anything.
'does_not_conform' would be a reason to look closer, not evidence of fabrication: state totals are shaped by state population sizes, estimation norms and rounding conventions.
